purpose: Vorapaxar is used to lower the risk of heart attack, stroke, and other serious heart and blood vessel problems in people who have already had a heart attack or have blockages in the arteries of their legs. It is used along with aspirin or another blood thinner called clopidogrel. It helps protect people who are at high risk for another dangerous heart or blood vessel event.
how_it_works: Your blood contains tiny cells called platelets that clump together to form clots. Vorapaxar blocks a specific signal on platelets called PAR-1 that tells them to clump together. By blocking this signal, the medication helps prevent dangerous clots from forming in your arteries, which can cause heart attacks or strokes.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is bleeding, which can range from minor cuts taking longer to stop bleeding to more serious internal bleeding. You may also notice bruising more easily than usual. Some people experience anemia, which means low red blood cell levels, making them feel tired or weak.
warnings: This medication can cause serious or life-threatening bleeding, especially in the brain. Do not take vorapaxar if you have ever had a stroke or a mini-stroke (TIA) because the risk of brain bleeding is very high. Always tell all your doctors and dentists you are on this medication. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can increase your risk of a heart attack. Avoid activities that could cause injury and be cautious with other medications that can increase bleeding, such as NSAIDs like ibuprofen.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 2.08 mg tablet taken by mouth once a day, with or without food. It is almost always taken together with aspirin or clopidogrel as directed by your doctor. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember.
